parsed.why: No trans-specific offence, facilities ban or documented targeting; same-sex conduct legal. Hate-crime enforcement gap and absent gender-identity protections, but regional court ruling and reopened prosecutions show recourse eventually works. Well-documented state: silence on trans issues reads mildly positive.

Courts struck surgery prerequisite and toilet ban, cross-dressing legal, but no anti-discrimination or hate-crime law, reported facility abuse by public, dated customs abuse, and visitor document handling unresolved.

No criminalisation, no facilities bans, society described as invisibility not hostility; but no anti-discrimination law and police dismiss trans victims' complaints using the male ID marker, producing documented impunity for anti-trans violence.

Sex-at-birth passport and visa screening refuses/strands travellers, facility bans with criminal trespass in some states, custody abuse and official threat-framing; partly offset by protective states, hate-crime statute and enjoining courts.

Gender nonconformity itself criminal under uncodified sharia; traveller arrested at airport for pre-arrival posts; trans woman died in custody after beating; mass lashings; deportation; no recognition or recourse.
